title: Judgment In P Jayaraj Vs R Saroja, 2007 ... vs R Saroja on 22 November, 2012
full_text: Judgment In P Jayaraj Vs R Saroja, 2007 ... vs R Saroja on 22 November, 2012 IN THE COURT OF SH. SHAILENDER MALIK : ACMM/01, NORTH EAST, KARKARDOOMA COURTS : DELHI Gopal Verma : Vimal Sharma CC No. : 538/10 U/s : 138 of N I Act PS : Shahdara JUDGEMENT 1 Serial No of the case 538/10 2 Date of institution of the case 10.11.2010 3 Name of the complainant Sh. Gopal Verma 4 Name of accused, parentage & Vimal Sharma, s/o Sh. R.D. Address Sharma, R/o A,107,Gali No. 2, West Nathu Colony, Shahdara, Delhi. 5 Offence complained of or U/S: 138 N I Act proved 6 Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty. 7 Date of reserve for order 26.10.2012 8 Final order Acquitted 9 Date of Judgment 22.11.2012 BRIEF REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE : ­ Cc no. 538/10 page 1 of 12 pages This is the complaint filed for the offence under section 138 N. I. Act with the allegations that accused Vimal Sharma in partial discharge of his legal enforceable debt and liability towards the complainant, issued a cheque baring no. 209676 dtd. 30.08.2010 of Rs. 60,000/­ drawn on "Delhi Nagrik Sahkari Bank Ltd." It is stated that accused had assured at the time of issuing the above said cheque that same will be duly encashed upon its presentation . It is stated that complainant when deposited the said cheque for encashment with his bankers, same returned dishonoured with remarks "Accounts Closed". It is stated that upon receipt of memo regarding dishonour of cheque complainant stated to have issued legal notice on 20.09.2010 by registered post as well as UPC. It is stated that legal notice sent through registered AD to the correct address of the accused returned with the remarks "Unclaimed RTS". It is stated that UPC however, has been duly served . It is stated that despite service of legal notice accused id not make the payment within prescribed period hence the present complaint was filed. After filing of the present complaint, pre summoning evidence was recorded and considering the pre summoning evidence Ld. Predecessor of this court vide order dtd. 31.3.2011, ordered for summoning of the accused for offence under section 138 N. I. Act. After the issuance of summons, accused did not appear and warrants were issued and ultimately when process under section 82 Cc no. 538/10 page 2 of 12 pages Cr.P.C was ordered to be issued, accused appeared and process was dropped and accused was admitted to bail. During the course of the proceedings parties entered into a settlement regarding which statement was recorded on 10.02.2012. However, accused did not make the payment as per settlement and therefore, notice of accusation for offence under section 138 N.I. Act was framed against the accused vide order dtd. 20.09.2012, to which accused pleaded not guilty and has taken the defence that he had not received any legal notice and has not filled the particulars of the cheque. Accused further says that cheque was given for security purpose to Balaji Finance only . In order to substantiate the charge complainant was called upon in witness box and in the evidence complainant in his affidavit of examination in chief has testified all those facts as are stated in his complaint and proved cheque, returning memo, legal notice, UPC, Regd. Postal envelope Etc. CW1 was duly cross examined wherein complainant has admitted that accused has taken a loan of Rs. 40,000/­ from M/s Shree Balaji Finance, and had paid the same by making full and final payment in Dwarka Courts. However complainant has denied that cheque in question was part and parcel of the cheque of the loan taken from M/s Shree Balaji Finance. CW1 was also confronted from his affidavit of examination in chief when he deposes that he had stated in his affidavit of examination in chief that he lent Rs. 60,000/­ as loan to the accused Cc no. 538/10 page 3 of 12 pages as this fact was not so mentioned in complaint or in his affidavit. CW1 has further stated in his cross examination that he cannot specify the exact date as to when he got issued his legal notice and he also do not remember as to by which mode he has sent the legal notice through his counsel. CW1 further says that he cannot specify any proof of delivery of legal notice on record. CW1 denied the suggestion that accused has not been served with the legal notice or that the complaint is time barred or that he has filed a false UPC slip. Complainant thereafter closed the CE. Statement of accused was recorded in terms of the provisions of section 281 CrPC, wherein accused has denied the evidence came on the record and has stated that he had never received any legal notice. Complaint is false and time barred. It is further stated that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case. Accused further states that he has already paid the settlement amount to M/s Shree Balaji Finance and cheque in question Ex CW1/A was given to the complainant for security purpose and same has been misused by the complainant. No evidence has been led in defence. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the complainant and Ld. Counsel for the accused. I have also gone through the written arguments filed on behalf of accused. It is argued by Ld. Counsel for the Cc no. 538/10 page 4 of 12 pages complainant that case of complainant is fully proved on the record and the plea of the accused that complaint is time barred is not sustainable in facts. Moreover, service of legal notice on the accused is proved with the help of UPC Ex CW1/D and there is a presumption of due service of notice when same is sent on the proper address of the accused. On the other hand it is argued by Ld. Counsel for the accused that legal notice has not been served upon the accused. It is argued that admittedly notice has not been served by registered post and only on the basis of UPC slip it cannot be presumed that notice has been served upon the accused. Moreover it is submitted that case is time barred and cheque is not for enforceable debt or liability. Ld. Counsel has relied upon the judgment in P JAYARAJ Vs R SAROJA , 2007 (1) DCR 562, JOSE Vs JOY, 2009 (1) Crl Court Cases 211, HDFC BANK LTD. Vs AMIT KUMAR SINGH, Crl. Rev. Pet. 296/09 (Hon'ble High Court of Delhi). Having heard the submissions at bar and having gone through the record carefully. Let us first discuss the legal requirement for proving charge of offence u/s 138 N. I. Act, from a reading of the said section, it is very clear that in order to attract the provisions thereof a cheque which is dishonored will have to be drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with the banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part of any debt or other liability. It is only Cc no. 538/10 page 5 of 12 pages such a cheque which is dishonored which would attract the provisions of Section 138 of the above Act against the drawer of the cheque. Section 138 and clauses (a), (b) and (c) to the proviso thereof indicate that a cheque has to be presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier. Clause (b) indicates that the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, has to make demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 30 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid and clause (c) provides that if the drawer of the cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or to the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of receipt of the said notice, the payee or the holder of the cheque may file a complaint under Section 142 of the Act in the manner prescribed. So merely on account of the fact that any cheque has been dishonored, no offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act can be said to have been made out unless the payee or the holder of the cheque makes a demand for payment of the amount of money by giving a notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid and drawer of the said cheque fails to make the payment of the amount of money to the payee or to the holder of the cheque within fifteen days of the receipt of the notice. Cc no. 538/10 page 6 of 12 pages So perusal of section 138 & 139 & 142 of Act will make clear that following are ingredients are required to invoke liability of section 138 N. I. Act: (i) a person must have drawn a cheque on an account maintained by him in a bank for payment of a certain amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge of any debt or other liability; (ii) That cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier; (iii) that cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because the amount of money standing to the credit of the account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with the bank; (iv) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within 15 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; Cc no. 538/10 page 7 of 12 pages (v) The drawer of such cheque fails to make payment of the said amount of money to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice. Service of a notice, it is trite, is imperative in character for maintaining a complaint. It creates a legal fiction. Operation of Section 138 of the Act is limited by the proviso. When the proviso applies, the main Section would not. Unless a notice is served in conformity with Proviso (b) appended to Section 138 of the Act, the complaint petition would not be maintainable. Because very cause of action for filling a complaint for offence under section 138 N I Act arises only when after dishonor of cheque, complainant sent legal demand notice within prescribed period & it is when accused despite being served with such notice failed to pay cheque amount within prescribed period, complaint is maintainable. In this context, the question as to whether such a notice has been served upon the proper address of accused is a question of fact. For this it is required on the part of complainant not only to make adequate averments in the complaint itself that the notice of demand, as required by Section 138 , stands served on the accused, but also to prove it. Although under Section 114 of the Evidence Act, a Court may presume that in the common course of natural event the communication would have been delivered at the address of the Cc no. 538/10 page 8 of 12 pages addressee. This apart section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, raises a presumption that such a notice stands served on the addressee. However it be also noted that such presumptions of fact either under section 114 of Evidence Act or under section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 are rebuttable in nature & complainant has duty to adduce evidence of either actual service of notice or he may take the risk of proving the service of notice by relying on the legal presumption. In the latter case, it would be sufficient for the complainant to adduce evidence to show that a notice was sent by registered post to the accused and that the address to which the notice was sent was the correct address. In present case admittedly legal notice has not been served by registered post, so far as UPC is concerned, same has not been proved by evidence of postal official, specifically when accused has denied that he has never been served with legal notice. As stated above the presumption, which Section 27 raises, is a rebuttable presumption and if the accused, either by entering into witness box or by any other means, denies receipt of such a notice, the presumption would stand rebutted. In that case it is imperative for complainant to prove service of legal notice on accused by positive evidence and not only on the basis of presumption. It be kept in mind that initial onus of proof, is always on complainant, to prove all necessary ingredients of offence, Present is a case where service of legal notice is not sought to be proved by registered post, because complainant has admittedly Cc no. 538/10 page 9 of 12 pages stated in complaint and also deposed on oath in Para 5 of his affidavit of his examination in chief, that on receipt of information that the said cheque dishonoured, complainant within statutory period sent legal notice dt. 20.09.10 through Registered post & UPC. In Para 6 of his affidavit, complainant testifies that legal notice sent through Registered post was not served on accused & received back with remarks "Unclaimed RTS". It is further stated that service of notice is to be effected on the accused. While legal notice sent through UPC has been delivered...." UPC Slip is Ex. Cw 1/D which is of 22­0910 & not of 20­09­10. So as per complainant himself, service of legal notice is only by UPC, whereas service has not been effected by registered post, in this regard it is appropriate to mention that in State of Maharashtra v. Rashid Babubhai Mulani AIR 2006 SC 825 : 2006 (1) Supreme 47 it was observed by Apex Court in Para 14 of Judgment as "A certificate of posting obtained by a sender is not comparable to a receipt for sending a communication by registered post. When a letter is sent by registered post, a receipt with serial number is issued and a record is maintained by the Post Office. But when a mere certificate of posting is sought, no record is maintained by the Post Office either about the receipt of the letter or the certificate issued. The ease with which such certificates can be procured by affixing ante­dated seal with the connivance of any employee of the Post Office is a matter of concern. The Department of Posts may have to evolve some procedure whereby a record in regard to the issuance of certificates is regularly maintained showing Cc no. 538/10 page 10 of 12 pages a serial number, date, sender's name and addressee's name to avoid misuse. In the absence of such a record, a certificate of posting may be of very little assistance, where the dispatch of such communications is disputed or denied as in this case." In Kumbhar v. Nanalal AIR 1988 Guj. 5, it was held by Hon'ble Gujarat High Court that in case of notice sent under certificate of posting, it cannot be deemed to have been served. Ld. Counsel for the accused has rightly relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in HDFC Bank Ltd. Vs. Amit Kumar Singh , in which our High Court has also discussed the requirement of proof of due service of notice. In present case also when accused has specifically denied to have received legal notice & admittedly UPC is of 22­09­10 & not of same date of Notice i.e 20­09­10, service is not from registered post, then it was necessary for complainant to prove due service of notice upon accused by examining post official to properly prove UPC, proof is proof¸ proof of a fact as per section of 3 of Evidence Act , is when, after considering the matters before it, the Court either believes it to exist, or consider its existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case, to act upon the supposition that it exists. What is required is production of such materials on which the Court can reasonably act to reach the supposition that a fact exists. Fact can be proved with help of rebuttable presumption, specifically when accused has denied that particular fact. Thus for reasons discussed above I find, that complainant has failed to prove most essential ingredient of Cc no. 538/10 page 11 of 12 pages offence u/s 138 N I Act, it is not proved that accused was served with notice, thus complaint is not legally not maintainable, therefore dismissed without discussing other facts, as a consequence thereof accused is acquitted of the charged offence. Bail bond/Surety bond of accused if lying on record are cancelled and discharged. File be consigned to record room. (ANNOUCNED IN THE OPEN COURT ON 22.11.2012) (SHAILENDER MALIK) ACMM/01/NORTH EAST, KARKARDOOMA COURT DELHI/ 22.11.2012 Cc no. 538/10 page 12 of 12 pages
